_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide and fisheries-literature sources (not a validated regional survey), for the Azores' mid-Atlantic volcanic seamount fauna, which is genuinely different from mainland Portugal: fewer Diplodus/Sparus-type seabream, more amberjack, blacktail comber and pelagic-adjacent structure species. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law.

species.note: The Azores' headline spearfishing target. Sedentary once it finds a good seamount or drop-off - hold a spot and it comes back. Deeper and more current-exposed than most Mediterranean reef species; wants a real drop-off, not gentle relief.
Sits shallower in the water column than greater amberjack - surface to mid-water rather than hard on the bottom - and is more often found over open structure than deep in it.
The Azores' most heavily landed grouper-family fish - small, resident, tight to rocky structure year round. A bread-and-butter fish here, not a trophy.
Warm-season visitor, mid-water over structure rather than resident in it - relief matters less to this species than to the bottom-dwellers on this list.
Same wary, deep-holding predator behaviour as its Mediterranean range further east - drop-offs and current-swept points, not calm bays.
One of the common Azorean bream, mixed rocky/coarse ground - less structure-bound than dentex, more tolerant of open coarse bottom.

_legal_note: Legal rules live in legal/PT.json and apply nationally - Portugal's mainland size/season entries do not necessarily match Azorean regional measures. One important regional rule this app cannot currently show: the Regional Government of the Azores prohibits spearfishing for dusky grouper (Epinephelus marginatus, 'mero') outright, which is why it is deliberately not listed as a target species here even though it is present and commonly seen. Always check current Azorean regional rules, not just national PT ones, before diving.
